Series::isnan¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::isnan() const -> Series

What It Does¶

isnan() returns a boolean mask that is true exactly where a lane contains nan.

This is the sharpest detector in the numeric-state family: it does not match finite numbers, and it does not match infinities.

Returns¶

Series A boolean Series with the same shape as self.

Gradient¶

isnan() is a boolean classification surface, not a differentiable numeric transform.

Examples¶

Example 1. Only the nan lane is marked as true.

auto special = pluss::make_series({
    -std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity(),
    -1.0,
    std::numeric_limits<double>::quiet_NaN(),
    0.0,
    std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity(),
});

std::cout << special.isnan();

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[false, false, true, false, false]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • isnan() does not catch infinities.

  • Use it when missing or undefined numeric state is the concern specifically.

  • If the next step is cleanup, pair it with nan_to_num().

Summary¶

Use isnan() when the question is specifically whether a value is undefined as nan.

See Also¶

  • Series::isinf: catches infinities instead.

  • Series::isfinite: broad finite/non-finite mask.

  • Series::nan_to_num: replace nan and infinities with explicit numeric substitutes.
